sections.body_md: This classroom prototype connects a research brief, literature review, experiment design, exported code, uploaded measurements, and a draft. In the bundled reference run, SGD accuracy was {{metric:m0}} and Adam accuracy was {{metric:m2}}. The values were equal; the run does not establish optimizer superiority.
The objective is to demonstrate a traceable research workflow with explicit user approval between stages. This draft is an educational artifact, not a novel optimization result.

Adam uses adaptive moment estimates {{cite:arxiv_1412_6980}}. Decoupled weight decay addresses a different regularization issue {{cite:arxiv_1711_05101}}. Hyperparameter choices require care {{cite:arxiv_1803_09820}}. These references do not validate performance claims on the present dataset.

The exported CPU script compares SGD and Adam MLP classifiers on Iris using a shared stratified split and a scaler fitted on training data. Execution configuration and environment are retained in the uploaded result file.

The uploaded run reports SGD accuracy {{metric:m0}}, SGD macro F1 {{metric:m1}}, Adam accuracy {{metric:m2}}, and Adam macro F1 {{metric:m3}}. Both fits reported convergence warnings. This is a single-seed, single-split integration example.

The workflow preserves approved inputs and connects measurements to a draft. The reference run provides no observed accuracy advantage for Adam. Repeated seeds and convergence checks would be needed before broader conclusions.
